words.enDefinition: local passenger services available to the public, such as buses and urban trains

examples.en: I started using public transit when I moved into a flat near campus.
examples.zh: 搬进学校附近的公寓后，我开始坐「公共交通」。

examples.en: The city added a public transit route that stops outside the new library.
examples.zh: 市里新增了一条经过新图书馆门口的「公共交通」线路。

words.enDefinition: an organization that runs or oversees public transportation services in an area

examples.en: The transit agency posted a map showing which bus stops had moved.
examples.zh: 「公共交通管理机构」发了一张图，标出哪些公交站搬到了别处。

examples.en: I checked the transit agency website after seeing a notice at the station.
examples.zh: 在车站看到通知后，我去查了「公共交通管理机构」的网站。

words.enDefinition: a bus operating within a community or area and typically stopping frequently

examples.en: I took a local bus to the supermarket after my afternoon lecture.
examples.zh: 下午下课后，我坐「本地公交车」去了超市。

examples.en: The local bus stops outside the student flats on its way downtown.
examples.zh: 「本地公交车」开往市中心时会在学生公寓外停靠。

words.enDefinition: a bus service that takes less time by skipping stops or using a faster route

examples.en: I took the express bus because it skipped several stops near campus.
examples.zh: 我坐「快速公交车」，因为它会跳过学校附近的几站。

examples.en: The express bus reaches the city centre before the regular service does.
examples.zh: 「快速公交车」比普通班次更早到市中心。

words.enDefinition: a bus that serves fewer stops on its route than an ordinary service does

examples.en: I checked whether the limited-stop bus would stop near my evening class.
examples.zh: 我查了「少停站公交车」会不会在我上晚课的地方附近停靠。

examples.en: The limited-stop bus served the hospital but skipped our smaller campus stop.
examples.zh: 「少停站公交车」会停靠医院站，但跳过了我们学校那个小站。

words.enDefinition: a transport service scheduled to call at every regular stop on the route

examples.en: The sign showed that this was an all-stops service to the city centre.
examples.zh: 牌子显示，这是去市中心「各站都停的班次」。

examples.en: I chose the all-stops service because the express skipped the student residence.
examples.zh: 快车跳过了学生公寓站，所以我选了「各站都停的班次」。

words.enDefinition: a bus that operates late at night, often after regular services stop

examples.en: I took the night bus home after the campus film screening ended.
examples.zh: 校园电影放映结束后，我坐「夜间公交车」回家。

examples.en: The night bus uses a different stop on the other side of the road.
examples.zh: 「夜间公交车」停靠的是马路对面的另一个站。

words.enDefinition: a bus operating instead of another service that is temporarily unavailable

examples.en: A replacement bus took us past the stations affected by weekend track work.
examples.zh: 一辆「临时代运公交车」把我们带过周末轨道施工影响的几个车站。

examples.en: We found the replacement bus outside the station after following the temporary signs.
examples.zh: 我们顺着临时指示牌，在车站外找到了「临时代运公交车」。

words.enDefinition: a high-capacity bus service designed for faster, more reliable trips, often using dedicated lanes

examples.en: The city opened a bus rapid transit route from campus to the hospital.
examples.zh: 市里开了一条从校区到医院的「快速公交系统」线路。

examples.en: Our class compared bus rapid transit with ordinary routes that use shared lanes.
examples.zh: 我们在课上比较了「快速公交系统」和走混合车道的普通线路。

collocations: build a bus rapid transit corridor

words.enDefinition: a long bus with sections joined by a flexible joint so it can turn

examples.en: An articulated bus arrived just as our lecture group reached the crowded stop.
examples.zh: 我们班一到拥挤的站台，一辆「铰接式公交车」就来了。

examples.en: I stood near the middle of the articulated bus because the front was full.
examples.zh: 车前部挤满了，我站在「铰接式公交车」中段附近。

words.enDefinition: an electric bus that runs on roads and draws power from overhead wires

examples.en: Our trolleybus passed under a row of wires on the edge of town.
examples.zh: 我们的「无轨电车」在城边从一排电线下经过。

examples.en: The city map gave the trolleybus its own colour alongside regular bus routes.
examples.zh: 城市地图给「无轨电车」用了单独的颜色，与普通公交线路区分。

words.enDefinition: an urban passenger vehicle running on rails, often along city streets

examples.en: We got the tram from the market stop to the university entrance.
examples.zh: 我们从市场站坐「有轨电车」到了学校入口。

examples.en: The tram slowed as it went through the crowded shopping street downtown.
examples.zh: 「有轨电车」经过市中心人多的商业街时减了速。

words.enDefinition: an urban rail system using relatively light vehicles, often at street level or on separate tracks

examples.en: I used light rail to get across town for my afternoon placement.
examples.zh: 我坐「轻轨」穿过市区，去参加下午的实习。

examples.en: The light rail stops beside the newer campus instead of crossing the river.
examples.zh: 「轻轨」停在新一些的校区旁边，不往河对岸开。

words.enDefinition: an urban rapid rail system, which may run underground, above ground or both

examples.en: I took the metro to the student museum because it was raining.
examples.zh: 下雨了，我坐「城市地铁」去了学生博物馆。

examples.en: The metro was faster than the bus during the morning traffic that day.
examples.zh: 那天早上车多的时候，「城市地铁」比公交更快。

words.enDefinition: a map showing the routes, stops and connections in a public transport network

examples.en: The transit map near the entrance showed three ways to reach campus.
examples.zh: 入口附近的「公共交通线路图」标出了到学校的三种走法。

examples.en: I used the transit map to find a connection after the lecture.
examples.zh: 下课后，我看了「公共交通线路图」找换乘线路。

words.enDefinition: the path and sequence of stops followed by a scheduled bus service

examples.en: I checked which bus route went past the building for my placement.
examples.zh: 我查了哪条「公交线路」会经过我实习的那栋楼。

examples.en: The city changed one bus route after the road near campus closed.
examples.zh: 学校附近道路封闭后，市里调整了一条「公交线路」。

words.enDefinition: the number or code identifying a particular transport route

examples.en: I copied the route number from the screen before leaving the stop.
examples.zh: 离开站台前，我记下了屏幕上的「公交线路编号」。

examples.en: The driver asked which route number was printed on my travel directions.
examples.zh: 司机问我乘车路线说明上印的是哪个「公交线路编号」。

words.enDefinition: a temporary change to a transport route to avoid a blocked section

examples.en: The notice showed a route diversion around the construction near the library.
examples.zh: 通知说，图书馆附近施工期间「线路会临时绕行」。

examples.en: The driver announced a route diversion because the market street was closed.
examples.zh: 市场那条街封了，司机通知大家「线路会临时绕行」。

words.enDefinition: a notice warning travellers about changes or problems affecting a transport service

examples.en: I received a service alert while waiting for the bus after class.
examples.zh: 下课后等公交时，我收到一条「运营变动提醒」。

examples.en: The service alert explained which stops were closed during the street festival.
examples.zh: 「运营变动提醒」说明街头节庆期间哪些站会关闭。

words.enDefinition: a stop used for a limited period while normal arrangements have changed

examples.en: A yellow sign pointed to the temporary stop beside the university gate.
examples.zh: 一个黄色牌子指向学校大门旁的「临时停靠站」。

examples.en: The temporary stop was across the road while the shelter was being repaired.
examples.zh: 候车亭维修期间，「临时停靠站」设在马路对面。

words.enDefinition: a stop that has been moved to a different place from its former location

examples.en: The notice gave a map of the relocated stop behind the library.
examples.zh: 通知附了地图，标出图书馆后面的「已迁移的停靠站」。

examples.en: I checked whether the relocated stop still served buses heading toward campus.
examples.zh: 我确认了「已迁移的停靠站」是否还停开往学校的公交车。

collocations: a map of the relocated stop

words.enDefinition: the vertical post that supports a bus stop sign or route information

examples.en: I found the revised timetable attached to the bus stop pole near the café.
examples.zh: 我发现改过的时刻表贴在咖啡馆附近的「公交站牌立杆」上。

examples.en: The bus stop pole had a small code below the route numbers.
examples.zh: 「公交站牌立杆」在线路编号下面写了一小行代码。

collocations: read a notice on the bus stop pole
stand beside the bus stop pole
a clearly marked bus stop pole

words.enDefinition: a covered structure that provides protection while people wait for a bus

examples.en: We moved into the bus shelter when it started raining after class.
examples.zh: 下课后开始下雨，我们就走进了「公交候车亭」。

examples.en: The bus shelter beside campus had a seat and a small route map.
examples.zh: 学校旁边的「公交候车亭」里有座位，还有张小线路图。

words.enDefinition: a marked stopping space that a bus pulls into to pick up or drop off passengers

examples.en: The driver pulled into the bus bay while passengers waited by the market.
examples.zh: 乘客在市场旁等候时，司机把车开进了「公交停靠港湾」。

examples.en: The bus bay was set back from the main traffic lane near campus.
examples.zh: 学校附近的「公交停靠港湾」向主车道外侧凹进去。

words.enDefinition: a lane reserved mainly for buses according to local rules

examples.en: Our bus moved quickly in the bus lane beside the morning traffic.
examples.zh: 早上车多，我们的车沿着「公交专用车道」开得很快。

examples.en: The window faced the bus lane on the road outside my flat.
examples.zh: 窗户正对着公寓外道路上的「公交专用车道」。

words.enDefinition: a facility where several bus routes begin or end and passengers can change services

examples.en: We changed buses at the bus terminal closest to the main campus.
examples.zh: 我们在离主校区最近的「公交总站」换了车。

examples.en: I checked the departure board inside the bus terminal after buying a ticket.
examples.zh: 买好票后，我在「公交总站」里面看了发车牌。

collocations: change buses at a bus terminal

words.enDefinition: a place where buses are kept, maintained or prepared when they are not serving passengers

examples.en: The route map showed a bus depot beside the industrial park outside town.
examples.zh: 线路图标出了城外工业园旁边的「公交车辆场站」。

examples.en: I wondered why the empty bus was heading toward the bus depot.
examples.zh: 我想知道那辆空车为什么开往「公交车辆场站」。

collocations: a maintenance area at a bus depot

words.enDefinition: a unique identifier for a particular bus stop used in timetables or travel apps

examples.en: I entered the bus stop code to see when the next service would arrive.
examples.zh: 我输入「公交站查询编码」，查看下一班什么时候到。

examples.en: The bus stop code was printed at the bottom of the information panel.
examples.zh: 「公交站查询编码」印在信息牌的最下面。

collocations: look up a bus stop code

words.enDefinition: a stop where a vehicle stops only when a passenger signals or requests it

examples.en: The small stop outside our village was marked as a request stop.
examples.zh: 我们村外那个小站标的是「按需停靠站」。

examples.en: I asked the driver how to get off at the next request stop.
examples.zh: 我问司机，想在下一个「按需停靠站」下车该怎么做。

collocations: get off at a request stop

words.enDefinition: a spoken or recorded message identifying the next or current stop

examples.en: The stop announcement helped me recognize the street on my first trip.
examples.zh: 第一次坐这趟车时，我靠「到站播报」认出了那条街。

examples.en: I heard the stop announcement just before the bus turned toward campus.
examples.zh: 公交车拐往学校前，我听到了「到站播报」。

words.enDefinition: a button passengers press to ask the driver to stop at the next designated stop

examples.en: The stop request button was beside the window above my seat.
examples.zh: 「请求下车按钮」在我座位上方、靠窗的位置。

examples.en: I pressed the stop request button after the announcement for the museum.
examples.zh: 听到博物馆站的播报后，我按了「请求下车按钮」。

words.enDefinition: to register the start of a transit trip by touching a card or device to a reader

examples.en: I watched someone tap on at the front of the bus in Sydney.
examples.zh: 在悉尼，我看到有人「上车时刷卡」，读卡器就在公交车前门。

examples.en: The station symbol showed passengers where to tap on before boarding the tram.
examples.zh: 车站标识告诉乘客，上有轨电车前到哪里「刷卡」。

words.enDefinition: to register the end of a transit trip by touching a card or device to a reader

examples.en: I saw people tap off just before stepping down from the Sydney bus.
examples.zh: 我看到悉尼公交车上的乘客「下车时刷卡」，刷完才走下车。

examples.en: The notice explained why people tap off at that station after their journey.
examples.zh: 通知说明了为什么在那个车站，行程结束要「感应刷卡」。

words.enDefinition: an entry or exit barrier that opens after a fare or ticket has been verified

examples.en: I took my card out before reaching the fare gate at the station.
examples.zh: 我到车站的「检票闸机」前就把卡拿了出来。

examples.en: The fare gate stayed closed until the reader recognized my paper ticket.
examples.zh: 读卡设备识别我的纸票后，「检票闸机」才打开。

collocations: line up at the fare gate

words.enDefinition: a device that checks or records the validity of a ticket for travel

examples.en: I held the paper ticket near the ticket validator at the tram stop.
examples.zh: 我在电车站把纸质车票靠近「验票机」。

examples.en: The ticket validator displayed a message after I presented my mobile ticket.
examples.zh: 我出示手机车票后，「验票机」显示了一条信息。

collocations: place a ticket on the ticket validator
a ticket validator on a tram

words.enDefinition: a device that reads a card or device to register a transit fare

examples.en: I held my card next to the fare reader by the bus door.
examples.zh: 我把卡靠近公交车门旁的「车费感应读卡器」。

examples.en: The fare reader flashed green before the screen showed the new balance.
examples.zh: 「车费感应读卡器」先闪起绿灯，随后屏幕显示了新余额。

collocations: tap a card on the fare reader
a fare reader at the gate

words.enDefinition: a check that passengers have paid or hold valid travel tickets

examples.en: Our tram stopped briefly while the staff carried out a fare inspection.
examples.zh: 工作人员做「车票稽查」时，我们坐的有轨电车短暂停了一下。

examples.en: I kept the mobile ticket open after hearing an announcement about fare inspection.
examples.zh: 听到「车票稽查」的通知后，我没关手机车票页面。

words.enDefinition: a transport employee who checks that passengers hold valid tickets or have paid the fare

examples.en: The fare inspector waited while I found the ticket in my email.
examples.zh: 我在邮件里找车票时，「查票员」等了一下。

examples.en: I asked the fare inspector whether my ticket covered the replacement bus.
examples.zh: 我问「查票员」这张票能不能坐代运公交。

collocations: show a ticket to a fare inspector

words.enDefinition: a card that can be used repeatedly to pay or record fares on public transport

examples.en: I bought a reusable transit card because I planned to take buses every week.
examples.zh: 我计划每周都坐公交，所以买了一张「可重复使用的公交卡」。

examples.en: The visitor office explained where to buy a reusable transit card near campus.
examples.zh: 访客服务处解释了学校附近去哪儿买「可重复使用的公交卡」。

words.enDefinition: a ticket displayed or stored on a phone or other mobile device

examples.en: The conductor scanned my mobile ticket from the screen of my phone.
examples.zh: 车上工作人员扫描了我手机屏幕上的「手机电子车票」。

examples.en: I downloaded the mobile ticket before going to the underground platform.
examples.zh: 去地下站台前，我下载了「手机电子车票」。

words.enDefinition: a printed ticket that can be shown or used for a journey

examples.en: I bought a paper ticket because my phone had run out of power.
examples.zh: 手机没电了，我买了一张「纸质车票」。

examples.en: The station machine printed a paper ticket and a separate payment receipt.
examples.zh: 车站机器打出一张「纸质车票」和一张单独的付款收据。

collocations: show a paper ticket at the gate

words.enDefinition: a ticket whose QR code can be scanned to confirm the passenger's right to travel

examples.en: I held the QR code ticket under the scanner at the tram stop.
examples.zh: 我在电车站把「二维码车票」放到扫描器下。

examples.en: The app asked me to open the QR code ticket before reaching the platform.
examples.zh: 应用提示我，在到站台之前打开「二维码车票」。

words.enDefinition: a transit pass that covers eligible trips for an academic semester

examples.en: My semester transit pass arrived after I confirmed my university registration online.
examples.zh: 我在网上确认大学注册后，收到了「学期公交乘车证」。

examples.en: The university showed me how the semester transit pass appeared in the app.
examples.zh: 学校给我看了「学期公交乘车证」在应用里是什么样。

words.enDefinition: a transit pass covering eligible trips during a month or monthly period

examples.en: I compared a monthly transit pass with the cost of separate bus fares.
examples.zh: 我比较了「月度公交乘车证」和单独买公交票的费用。

examples.en: The monthly transit pass covered the two lines I used for class.
examples.zh: 「月度公交乘车证」覆盖我上课要坐的两条线路。

collocations: travel with a monthly transit pass

words.enDefinition: a ticket allowing specified public transport journeys in a day or day-long period

examples.en: I bought a day pass for visiting several museums on Saturday afternoon.
examples.zh: 我买了张「一日乘车票」，周六下午去好几个博物馆。

examples.en: The driver showed me which part of the day pass gave its expiry time.
examples.zh: 司机给我看了「一日乘车票」上哪儿写着失效时间。

collocations: a day pass for the bus

words.enDefinition: a card holding a prepaid balance from which fares can be deducted

examples.en: The gate displayed the remaining credit on my stored-value card after the trip.
examples.zh: 乘车结束后，闸机显示了「储值乘车卡」的剩余金额。

examples.en: I asked whether my stored-value card worked on buses in that district.
examples.zh: 我问「储值乘车卡」能不能在那个区坐公交用。

collocations: load money onto a stored-value card

words.enDefinition: to add more money or value to a card used for transport fares

examples.en: The kiosk showed me where to reload a transit card before boarding.
examples.zh: 售票亭提示我上车前在哪里「为公交卡充值」。

examples.en: I needed to reload a transit card after seeing a low balance message.
examples.zh: 看到余额偏低的提示后，我得「为公交卡充值」。

collocations: reload a transit card at a kiosk
need to reload a transit card

words.enDefinition: a station or street machine that adds prepaid credit to a travel card

examples.en: The top-up machine showed my current balance after I inserted the card.
examples.zh: 我插入卡后，「公交卡充值机」显示了当前余额。

examples.en: I found the top-up machine just inside the subway entrance near campus.
examples.zh: 我在学校附近的地铁入口里面找到了「公交卡充值机」。

collocations: add money at a top-up machine

words.enDefinition: a machine from which passengers can buy or collect travel tickets

examples.en: I used the ticket machine to buy a pass before meeting my classmates.
examples.zh: 和同学碰面前，我用「自助售票机」买了张通票。

examples.en: The ticket machine had a different button for discounted student fares.
examples.zh: 「自助售票机」上学生优惠票价有单独的按钮。

collocations: buy a ticket from a ticket machine
a ticket machine at the entrance

words.enDefinition: a device on a bus or other vehicle used to collect cash fares

examples.en: I saw one passenger drop coins into the fare box after boarding.
examples.zh: 我看到一名乘客上车后把硬币投进「公交投币箱」。

examples.en: The driver pointed to the fare box when I asked where to pay.
examples.zh: 我问该在哪里付车费，司机指了指「公交投币箱」。

collocations: put coins in the fare box
a fare box beside the driver

words.enDefinition: the fare amount when a passenger pays for transport using cash

examples.en: I asked the driver whether the cash fare matched the price on the sign.
examples.zh: 我问司机，「现金车费」是不是和牌子上的价格一样。

examples.en: The notice listed the cash fare separately from the electronic card fare.
examples.zh: 通知把「现金车费」和电子卡票价分开列了。

words.enDefinition: a single price for eligible trips regardless of how far the passenger travels

examples.en: The bus leaflet said the route used a flat fare between all its stops.
examples.zh: 公交宣传单说，这条线各站之间都实行「全程统一车费」。

examples.en: I asked if the flat fare covered a trip from campus to the market.
examples.zh: 我问，从学校到市场的一程是否适用「全程统一车费」。

collocations: a flat fare for the route

words.enDefinition: a fare whose amount depends on the distance travelled

examples.en: The leaflet illustrated a distance-based fare using a short trip and a longer one.
examples.zh: 宣传单用一段短行程和一段长行程说明了「按距离计费的车费」。

examples.en: I asked how the distance-based fare was recorded on my trip history.
examples.zh: 我问「按距离计费的车费」在乘车记录里怎么显示。

words.enDefinition: an area used to determine the cost or validity of a transport journey

examples.en: I checked which fare zone included the station closest to my campus.
examples.zh: 我查了离学校最近的车站在哪个「票价分区」。

examples.en: The ticket shows the fare zone where it is valid for travel.
examples.zh: 车票上标出了可以使用的「票价分区」。

words.enDefinition: a price based on the fare zones covered by the passenger's trip

examples.en: The map helps travellers find the zone fare for a journey across town.
examples.zh: 这张图帮乘客查找横穿市区要付的「按区计费的车费」。

examples.en: I compared the zone fare for two routes to the museum.
examples.zh: 我比较了去博物馆的两条线路中「按区计费的车费」。

words.enDefinition: the dividing line between two different fare zones in a transport network

examples.en: The map showed a zone boundary just beyond the stop nearest campus.
examples.zh: 地图显示，离学校最近的站再过去一点就是「票价区边界」。

examples.en: We checked the zone boundary before deciding which ticket to buy for the train.
examples.zh: 我们先查看了「票价区边界」，再决定买哪种火车票。

collocations: a station on a zone boundary

words.enDefinition: a reduced fare offered to groups that meet the operator's eligibility conditions

examples.en: The machine displayed concession fare as a category beneath the standard adult price.
examples.zh: 售票机在标准成人票价下方单列了「特定人群优惠车费」。

examples.en: I asked which student documents were accepted for the concession fare in that city.
examples.zh: 我问在那个城市，乘车要享受「特定人群优惠车费」可用哪些学生证件。

words.enDefinition: a fare that applies when a passenger changes between eligible services during a trip

examples.en: I checked the transfer fare before changing from the bus to the tram.
examples.zh: 我从公交换乘电车前查了「换乘车费」。

examples.en: The fare guide listed a transfer fare for this particular pair of routes.
examples.zh: 票价指南列出了这两条线路之间的「换乘车费」。

words.enDefinition: permission to move onto an eligible connecting service without paying a separate fare

examples.en: I checked whether my bus ticket allowed a free transfer to the tram.
examples.zh: 我确认公交票能不能「免费换乘」电车。

examples.en: The app showed where a free transfer was available on that itinerary.
examples.zh: 应用显示这条行程上哪里可以「免费换乘」。

words.enDefinition: the time period during which a connecting trip can be counted under a transfer fare rule

examples.en: I checked the transfer window before deciding whether to stop for coffee.
examples.zh: 我先看了「换乘有效时段」，再决定要不要停下买咖啡。

examples.en: The receipt displayed the end of my transfer window beside the first fare.
examples.zh: 收据在第一段车费旁边印了我的「换乘有效时段」何时结束。

words.enDefinition: a location where travellers can change between routes or modes of transport

examples.en: The map marked the library as a transfer point between two bus routes.
examples.zh: 线路图把图书馆标为两条公交线路之间的「换乘点」。

examples.en: I waited at the transfer point just outside the entrance to the park.
examples.zh: 我在公园入口外的「换乘点」等车。

collocations: change buses at a transfer point

words.enDefinition: a station where passengers can change between several routes or transport services

examples.en: We changed to the metro at the interchange station near the market.
examples.zh: 我们在市场附近的「换乘站」换乘地铁。

examples.en: The interchange station has separate platforms for trams and underground trains.
examples.zh: 这座「换乘站」给有轨电车和地铁分别设了站台。

words.enDefinition: a major point where several different transport routes or modes meet

examples.en: The main transfer hub connects buses with two tram lines outside the station.
examples.zh: 主「交通换乘枢纽」在车站外把公交和两条有轨电车线路连在一起。

examples.en: The city moved the transfer hub closer to the central train station.
examples.zh: 市里把「交通换乘枢纽」搬得离中央火车站更近。

words.enDefinition: a limit on the total charged for eligible travel within a stated period

examples.en: I asked how the fare cap appeared in my online trip history.
examples.zh: 我问「车费累计上限」在网上的乘车记录里怎样显示。

examples.en: The visitor guide illustrated a fare cap using several journeys in one day.
examples.zh: 游客指南用同一天的几段行程说明了什么是「车费累计上限」。

words.enDefinition: a fare charged for travel during designated busier times

examples.en: The machine showed a peak fare for the time I had selected.
examples.zh: 售票机为我选的时段显示了「高峰时段车费」。

examples.en: I checked whether the price on my trip history was a peak fare.
examples.zh: 我核对了乘车记录上的价格是不是「高峰时段车费」。

words.enDefinition: a fare charged for travel outside an operator's designated busy times

examples.en: The app showed an off-peak fare beside the price for the earlier departure.
examples.zh: 应用在较早班次价格旁列出了「非高峰时段车费」。

examples.en: I asked which time the off-peak fare started in the local fare guide.
examples.zh: 我问当地车费指南规定「非高峰时段车费」从何时开始。

words.enDefinition: a service that takes passengers to a destination without requiring a change of vehicle

examples.en: I took a direct service to campus so I could keep reading on the bus.
examples.zh: 我坐了去学校的「直达班次」，可以继续在公交车上阅读。

examples.en: The route planner showed no direct service to the museum on Sundays.
examples.zh: 行程规划工具显示，周日没有去博物馆的「直达班次」。

words.enDefinition: a transport service that a passenger can change to in order to continue a journey

examples.en: I found the connecting service on the screen after getting off the tram.
examples.zh: 下了有轨电车后，我在屏幕上找到了「接续班次」。

examples.en: The guide showed where the connecting service would stop during the works.
examples.zh: 指南标出了施工期间「接续班次」在哪里停。

collocations: take a connecting service to campus

words.enDefinition: to switch from one transit line to another during a journey

examples.en: I had to change lines at the next station to reach the new campus.
examples.zh: 我要在下一站「换乘另一条线路」，才能到新校区。

examples.en: The route planner showed where we could change lines without leaving the station.
examples.zh: 行程规划工具标出了哪里不用出站就能「换乘另一条线路」。

words.enDefinition: to board a bus that does not take you in the direction or to the place intended

examples.en: I managed to get on the wrong bus after reading the route number too quickly.
examples.zh: 我看公交线路编号看得太快，结果「坐错公交车」。

examples.en: The stop has two similar route signs, so it is easy to get on the wrong bus.
examples.zh: 站上有两个很像的线路牌，很容易「坐错公交车」。

collocations: accidentally get on the wrong bus
easy to get on the wrong bus
try not to get on the wrong bus

words.expression: get off at the next stop
words.lemma: get off at the next stop
words.enDefinition: to leave a vehicle at the stop immediately after your current position
acceptedEnVariants: get off at the next stop

examples.en: The driver told me to get off at the next stop for the market.
examples.zh: 司机说，去市场要「在下一站下车」。

examples.en: I decided to get off at the next stop and walk across the park.
examples.zh: 我决定「在下一站下车」，步行穿过公园。

collocations: need to get off at the next stop
ready to get off at the next stop
tell someone to get off at the next stop

words.enDefinition: to board the final scheduled bus for a route or destination

examples.en: We packed up early so we could catch the last bus home.
examples.zh: 我们提早收拾好东西，为的是「赶上末班公交」回家。

examples.en: I checked whether we could still catch the last bus after the film.
examples.zh: 我查了电影结束后还能不能「赶上末班公交」。

collocations: run to catch the last bus
leave in time to catch the last bus
hope to catch the last bus

words.enDefinition: to fail to reach the next planned service in time to board it

examples.en: I was worried I might miss a connection after the tram stopped.
examples.zh: 有轨电车停住后，我担心会「没赶上换乘班次」。

examples.en: The app showed another route if passengers happened to miss a connection.
examples.zh: 应用显示，乘客如果「没赶上换乘班次」，还有另一条线路。

collocations: cause someone to miss a connection
have enough time to avoid missing a connection

words.enDefinition: to enter a bus or other vehicle using its front door

examples.en: The sign asked passengers to board at the front during the festival.
examples.zh: 节庆期间，牌子请乘客「从前门上车」。

examples.en: The driver pointed to a notice saying to board at the front.
examples.zh: 司机指了指写着「从前门上车」的通知。

collocations: ask passengers to board at the front
board at the front of the bus
be ready to board at the front

words.enDefinition: a bus with a low passenger floor designed to make boarding easier

examples.en: The route map showed a low-floor bus symbol beside the weekend service.
examples.zh: 线路图在周末班次旁边用了「低地板公交车」标志。

examples.en: A low-floor bus arrived while we waited near the student residence entrance.
examples.zh: 我们在学生公寓入口附近等车时，来了一辆「低地板公交车」。

words.enDefinition: a bus that can lower one side or the front to reduce the boarding step

examples.en: The museum group boarded a kneeling bus from a raised curb outside.
examples.zh: 博物馆参观团从外面的高路缘上了一辆「可降低车身的公交车」。

examples.en: The guide explained how a kneeling bus makes the entrance lower for passengers.
examples.zh: 指南说明了「可降低车身的公交车」怎样帮乘客降低上车台阶。

collocations: a kneeling bus with a ramp

words.enDefinition: a designated area inside a vehicle where a passenger can travel in a wheelchair

examples.en: The bus had a wheelchair space beside the wider door near the driver.
examples.zh: 公交车靠近司机的宽门旁设有「车内轮椅乘客专区」。

examples.en: We left the wheelchair space clear when the other seats were full.
examples.zh: 其他座位坐满时，我们也让「车内轮椅乘客专区」保持空着。

words.enDefinition: a seat reserved or marked for passengers who may need it more

examples.en: I moved my bag off the priority seat when more passengers boarded.
examples.zh: 更多乘客上车时，我把包从「优先座位」上挪开。

examples.en: The priority seat had a bright blue sign above it near the door.
examples.zh: 靠门的「优先座位」上方有块亮蓝色的牌子。

words.enDefinition: a seat that folds down for use and up to leave more room

examples.en: I found a fold-down seat near the back of the crowded tram.
examples.zh: 我在拥挤的有轨电车后部找到了一个「可翻折座位」。

examples.en: The fold-down seat returned to its upright position when I stood up.
examples.zh: 我站起来后，「可翻折座位」就翻回了竖直位置。

words.enDefinition: space available for people who are not sitting, especially on transport

examples.en: There was only standing room when the bus reached our university stop.
examples.zh: 公交开到我们学校这站时，只剩「可以站的空间」。

examples.en: We let the next service go because it had very little standing room.
examples.zh: 下一班车几乎没有「可以站的空间」，我们就没上。

words.enDefinition: the earliest scheduled transit service on a route or day

examples.en: The first service left before the café at the station had opened.
examples.zh: 车站咖啡馆还没开门，「首班车」就发车了。

examples.en: I checked the first service before signing up for the early volunteer shift.
examples.zh: 报名参加早班志愿服务前，我查了「首班车」。

collocations: check the first service on Sunday

words.enDefinition: the final scheduled transit service on a route or day

examples.en: We asked whether the last service left from the same stop as usual.
examples.zh: 我们问「末班车」是否从平时那个站发车。

examples.en: The last service was already full by the time it reached our stop.
examples.zh: 「末班车」到我们那一站时，车里已经挤满了人。

collocations: check the time of the last service

words.enDefinition: how often buses, trains or other vehicles are scheduled to arrive or depart

examples.en: I checked the service frequency before choosing a placement across town.
examples.zh: 选择在城里另一头实习前，我查了「班次频率」。

examples.en: The leaflet showed a lower service frequency during the university holidays.
examples.zh: 宣传单显示，学校放假期间的「班次频率」较低。

words.enDefinition: a transport service operating often enough that waits are generally short

examples.en: Our local route had frequent service during the first week of term.
examples.zh: 新学期第一周，我们本地这条线路提供「发车频繁的服务」。

examples.en: I chose the tram because the route map described it as frequent service.
examples.zh: 我选有轨电车，因为线路图上说那条线是「发车频繁的服务」。

words.enDefinition: transport service scheduled for the busiest times of day

examples.en: The peak service stopped outside the library while other buses bypassed campus.
examples.zh: 「高峰时段运营」里，车停图书馆门口，其他公交则绕过学校。

examples.en: The leaflet showed how the peak service differed from the midday timetable.
examples.zh: 宣传单显示，「高峰时段运营」与中午的时刻表有什么不同。

words.enDefinition: transport service running outside an operator's busiest scheduled times

examples.en: The off-peak service took longer because it stopped at more local stations.
examples.zh: 「非高峰时段运营」下要多停几个小站，所以用时更长。

examples.en: I looked at the off-peak service before planning a trip after class.
examples.zh: 安排下课后出行之前，我查了「非高峰时段运营」。

words.enDefinition: the schedule followed by a transport service on Saturdays and Sundays

examples.en: I checked the weekend timetable before agreeing to meet my classmates on Sunday.
examples.zh: 答应周日和同学见面前，我查了「周末时刻表」。

examples.en: The weekend timetable listed a later first departure than the weekday one.
examples.zh: 「周末时刻表」列出的首班发车时间比工作日更晚。

words.enDefinition: a period or pattern with fewer transport services than normally run

examples.en: The notice warned of reduced service while one platform was being repaired.
examples.zh: 通知提醒，一个站台维修期间将「减班运行」。

examples.en: We left earlier because there would be reduced service over the holiday.
examples.zh: 假期会「减班运行」，所以我们提早出发了。

words.enDefinition: a different route used when the usual route is unavailable or less suitable

examples.en: The app showed an alternate route after the bus stop closed near campus.
examples.zh: 学校附近站点关闭后，应用显示了一条「备选线路」。

examples.en: I compared an alternate route with walking the entire way to the library.
examples.zh: 我把一条「备选线路」和全程步行到图书馆作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a scheduled service that turns back before reaching the usual end of its route

examples.en: A sign marked this as a short-turn service ending before the university stop.
examples.zh: 牌子注明这是「提前折返班次」，终点在学校站之前。

examples.en: I let the short-turn service go because it did not reach my destination.
examples.zh: 我没上这趟「提前折返班次」，因为它不到我的目的地。

words.enDefinition: not currently available for passengers to board or travel on

examples.en: The display said “out of service” when the empty bus passed us.
examples.zh: 空车经过时，显示屏写着「停止载客服务」。

examples.en: I missed the earlier bus because two vehicles on that route were out of service.
examples.zh: 那条线路上两辆车都「停止载客服务」，我没赶上前一班车。

collocations: mark a bus out of service
take a vehicle out of service
a bus that is out of service

words.enDefinition: a service travelling toward a designated centre or arrival terminal

examples.en: I had to cross the road to catch the inbound service toward downtown.
examples.zh: 我得过马路，去坐「往市中心方向的班次」。

examples.en: The plan placed the inbound service on a different platform during construction.
examples.zh: 施工期间，「往中心方向的班次」被安排到了另一个站台。

words.enDefinition: a service travelling away from a designated centre or starting terminal

examples.en: I took an outbound service from the city centre to the student residence.
examples.zh: 我从市中心坐「向外开的班次」去学生公寓。

examples.en: The app showed a delay on the outbound service beside the station map.
examples.zh: 应用在车站地图旁显示，有一趟「从中心向外的班次」晚点了。

words.enDefinition: the direction in which a vehicle is moving or is scheduled to go

examples.en: The map showed the direction of travel beside each line on the diagram.
examples.zh: 示意图在每条线路旁标出了「行驶方向」。

examples.en: I checked the direction of travel against the arrow on the station sign.
examples.zh: 我对照站内牌子上的箭头确认了「行驶方向」。

words.enDefinition: the final stop at one end of a scheduled transport route

examples.en: The driver announced that the next stop was the route terminus after the market.
examples.zh: 司机播报，过了市场之后下一站就是「线路终点站」。

examples.en: We found a covered waiting area next to the route terminus outside town.
examples.zh: 我们在城外「线路终点站」旁找到了有顶棚的候车区。

words.enDefinition: a disruption in which buses that should be spaced apart arrive close together

examples.en: We saw bus bunching when three vehicles arrived together after a long wait.
examples.zh: 等了很久后连来三辆车，我们碰到了「公交车扎堆到站」。

examples.en: The transit report mentioned bus bunching on the route outside our campus.
examples.zh: 交通报告提到，学校外那条线路出现了「公交车扎堆到站」。

collocations: bus bunching on a busy route

words.enDefinition: the planned time gap between consecutive vehicles serving the same route and direction

examples.en: I checked the scheduled headway to see how long the usual wait was.
examples.zh: 我查了「计划发车间隔」，看平时一般等多久。

examples.en: The scheduled headway was longer on Sundays than during the weekday rush.
examples.zh: 周日的「计划发车间隔」比工作日高峰期更长。

words.enDefinition: a scheduled vehicle or trip running later than planned

examples.en: We waited for a delayed service underneath the shelter outside the library.
examples.zh: 我们在图书馆外的候车亭等一趟「晚点班次」。

examples.en: The display showed the delayed service below two buses running on time.
examples.zh: 显示屏把那趟「晚点班次」列在两班准点车下面。

collocations: check the status of a delayed service
a notice about a delayed service

words.enDefinition: a scheduled trip or vehicle that the operator no longer plans to run

examples.en: The app marked a cancelled service after the road near campus closed.
examples.zh: 学校附近的路封闭后，应用标出了一趟「取消的班次」。

examples.en: I chose another route when the driver mentioned the cancelled service at the station.
examples.zh: 司机提到车站有一趟「取消的班次」后，我选了另一条线路。

collocations: a notice about a cancelled service

words.enDefinition: a scheduled interruption or restriction, often for maintenance, announced in advance

examples.en: The operator posted a planned service disruption for the weekend road repairs.
examples.zh: 运营商发布了周末修路期间「预先公布的运营中断」。

examples.en: I checked whether the planned service disruption would affect the bus to campus.
examples.zh: 我查了这次「预先公布的运营中断」会不会影响去学校的公交。

collocations: check for a planned service disruption

words.enDefinition: estimated arrival times updated using current information about moving vehicles

examples.en: The app shows real-time arrivals for stops close to the student flats.
examples.zh: 应用会显示学生公寓附近各站的「实时到站信息」。

examples.en: We checked real-time arrivals before deciding whether to walk to campus instead.
examples.zh: 我们先看了「实时到站信息」，再决定要不要改成走去学校。

words.enDefinition: departure times updated with current operational information rather than only the printed schedule

examples.en: I compared live departures for both tram lines while leaving the library.
examples.zh: 离开图书馆时，我比较了两条电车线路的「实时发车信息」。

examples.en: The screen stopped showing live departures during a brief power cut at the station.
examples.zh: 车站短暂停电时，屏幕停止显示「实时发车信息」。

words.enDefinition: a display counting down the time left until a service is due to leave

examples.en: The departure countdown reached one minute while I was walking toward the platform.
examples.zh: 我往站台走时，「发车倒计时」剩一分钟。

examples.en: The app updated the departure countdown after the tram arrived earlier than expected.
examples.zh: 电车比预计早到，应用更新了「发车倒计时」。

words.enDefinition: the time a particular vehicle or service is timetabled to depart

examples.en: The scheduled departure was written above the adjusted time on the app.
examples.zh: 应用把「计划发车时间」写在调整后的时间上方。

examples.en: I arrived ten minutes before the scheduled departure of the afternoon bus.
examples.zh: 我在下午那班公交「计划发车时间」前十分钟到了。

words.enDefinition: the currently predicted time when a vehicle will actually depart

examples.en: The estimated departure changed after the tram was held at the previous stop.
examples.zh: 电车在上一站停留后，「预计发车时间」变了。

examples.en: I refreshed the app to check the latest estimated departure for my route.
examples.zh: 我刷新应用，看这条线路最新的「预计发车时间」。

words.enDefinition: an estimate of when a vehicle will reach a particular stop or station

examples.en: The arrival prediction shifted while we waited at the university stop.
examples.zh: 我们在学校站等车时，「到站时间预测」变了。

examples.en: I compared the arrival prediction with the position of the bus on the map.
examples.zh: 我把「到站时间预测」和地图上的公交位置作了对照。

words.enDefinition: an app or display showing where buses are and when they may reach stops

examples.en: I opened the bus tracker before walking out of the student residence.
examples.zh: 走出学生公寓前，我打开了「公交位置跟踪工具」。

examples.en: The bus tracker showed the vehicle still waiting at its first stop.
examples.zh: 「公交位置跟踪工具」显示，那辆车还停在始发站。

words.enDefinition: a sign on a vehicle showing its destination and sometimes its route number

examples.en: I read the destination display before boarding the bus at the library.
examples.zh: 我在图书馆站上车前，先看了「终点站显示牌」。

examples.en: The destination display changed when the bus turned around at the last stop.
examples.zh: 公交车在末站掉头时，「终点站显示牌」上的内容变了。

words.enDefinition: a place where an urban tram picks up or drops off passengers

examples.en: We met at the tram stop nearest the design studio after class.
examples.zh: 下课后，我们在离设计工作室最近的「有轨电车站」碰面。

examples.en: The tram stop had a new map beside the ticket machine.
examples.zh: 「有轨电车站」的售票机旁有一张新地图。

words.enDefinition: a place where a road or path crosses railway tracks at the same height

examples.en: Our walking route took us past a level crossing outside the tram depot.
examples.zh: 我们走的路经过电车车场外的一个「平交道口」。

examples.en: The local map marked the level crossing near the sports field.
examples.zh: 本地地图标出了运动场附近的「平交道口」。

collocations: a level crossing near the station

words.enDefinition: an access point used to enter a transport station

examples.en: We agreed to meet at the station entrance after our morning lecture.
examples.zh: 早课后，我们约在「车站入口」见面。

examples.en: The station entrance by the park was closed during the repairs.
examples.zh: 维修期间，公园旁的「车站入口」关闭了。

words.enDefinition: a way out of a transport station that leads to the surrounding area

examples.en: I used a different station exit because the one by campus was closed.
examples.zh: 学校边上那个关了，我换了一个「车站出口」。

examples.en: The map showed which station exit led to the library through the park.
examples.zh: 地图标出了从哪个「车站出口」出去能经公园到图书馆。

collocations: follow signs to the station exit

words.enDefinition: the large public area inside a station that connects its entrances and facilities

examples.en: I met my classmate on the station concourse beside the ticket kiosk.
examples.zh: 我在「车站公共大厅」里的售票亭旁和同学见面。

examples.en: The station concourse had a temporary help desk during the street festival.
examples.zh: 街头节庆期间，「车站公共大厅」设了临时咨询台。

words.enDefinition: a line of passengers waiting to enter a vehicle

examples.en: I joined the boarding queue after checking that it was the correct route.
examples.zh: 我确认线路没错后，排进了「上车等候队伍」。

examples.en: The boarding queue extended past the shelter when two evening services were cancelled.
examples.zh: 两班晚间线路取消后，「上车等候队伍」排到了候车亭外面。

words.enDefinition: a stop where passengers board directly from the side of the road

examples.en: The replacement service used a curbside stop instead of the station's main platforms.
examples.zh: 代运班次使用「路缘停靠站」，没用车站的主站台。

examples.en: I checked the map for the curbside stop outside the student residence.
examples.zh: 我在地图上查了学生公寓外的「路缘停靠站」。

collocations: pick up passengers at a curbside stop

words.enDefinition: an announcement that passengers should expect the vehicle's left-side doors to open

examples.en: I heard “doors opening on the left” as the train approached our stop.
examples.zh: 车快到我们这一站时，我听到了「左侧车门开启」的播报。

examples.en: The screen showed “doors opening on the left” beside the station name.
examples.zh: 屏幕在站名旁显示「左侧车门开启」。

collocations: hear doors opening on the left
announce doors opening on the left
a message saying doors opening on the left

words.enDefinition: to keep your hand on a rail for support while standing or moving

examples.en: I tried to hold the handrail when the bus pulled away from the stop.
examples.zh: 公交驶离站台时，我尽量「扶住扶手」。

examples.en: The notice asked people to hold the handrail on the way down.
examples.zh: 通知请大家往下走时「扶住扶手」。

collocations: ask people to hold the handrail

words.enDefinition: to stand and offer your seat to a person who needs it more

examples.en: You can give up your seat if someone needs a place to sit.
examples.zh: 有人需要坐下的话，你可以「给别人让座」。

examples.en: The poster said, “Please give up your seat if another passenger needs it.”
examples.zh: 牌子请乘客在有人更需要座位时「给别人让座」。

collocations: offer to give up your seat
be willing to give up your seat
give up your seat to someone

words.enDefinition: a transport trip with many passengers and little free space

examples.en: I waited for the next bus instead of boarding the crowded service.
examples.zh: 我没上这趟「乘客拥挤的班次」，等了下一班公交。

examples.en: The route had a crowded service after the basketball match on campus.
examples.zh: 学校篮球比赛结束后，线路上有一趟「乘客拥挤的班次」。

collocations: wait for a less crowded service

words.enDefinition: a period when a particular transit stop is unavailable to passengers

examples.en: The app showed a stop closure outside the library until the following morning.
examples.zh: 应用显示，图书馆外「站点关闭」会持续到第二天早上。

examples.en: I read the stop closure notice before walking to the temporary stop.
examples.zh: 我先读了「站点关闭」通知，再走去临时站。

words.enDefinition: a tool that suggests ways to travel between locations using available routes

examples.en: I used a route planner to find the quickest trip home after class.
examples.zh: 下课后，我用「线路规划工具」找最快的回家路线。

examples.en: The route planner offered a bus connection instead of the usual tram.
examples.zh: 「线路规划工具」推荐了换乘公交，没推荐平时坐的电车。
